title: TechnicalService
description: Schema for technical service definitions in the commercial bank's target architecture. A technical service is the deployable unit that realises one or more business capabilities. Each service has a single owning team, a bounded data domain, and published API contracts consumed by dependent services.

id.description: Unique service identifier. SVC-001 to SVC-049 = domain services. SVC-050 to SVC-099 = cross-cutting shared services. SVC-100+ = foundation platform services.

name.description: Human-readable service name. Should be descriptive enough to convey the service's primary responsibility without abbreviation.

description.description: A precise description of what the service does, what data domain it owns, and its primary responsibilities. Should be self-contained — a new team member should understand the service's purpose from this field alone.

classification.description: Classifies the service's architectural role. domain_specific: realises a single business capability; owned by one domain team. cross_cutting: serves multiple capabilities as a shared service; owns a cross-capability concern (e.g. KYC, sanctions screening). foundation: platform-layer infrastructure used by all services (e.g. API gateway, event bus, identity management).

status.description: Lifecycle status of the service definition.

capability_mappings.description: One or more capability segments this service realises. Each mapping includes the capability ID, the realisation type, and which sub-capabilities are in scope.

capability_id.description: The capability or sub-capability ID from the capability map (e.g. CAP-001, CAP-001.04).

realisation_type.description: How this service maps to the capability. realises_parent: the service realises the retained parent (after sub-caps are promoted). realises_promoted_sub_capability: the service realises a single promoted sub-capability. realises_shared_sub_capability: the service realises a cross-capability shared concern. realises_retained_sub_capabilities: the service realises multiple retained sub-capabilities within a parent.

sub_capabilities_in_scope.description: List of sub-capability IDs included in this service's scope (for parent services with multiple retained sub-caps).

dependencies.description: Services this service depends on at runtime. Captures both hard blocking dependencies (payment cannot proceed without sanctions clearance) and soft dependencies (async event subscriptions).

service_id.description: The ID of the depended-upon service.

service_name.description: Human-readable name of the depended-upon service.

dependency_type.description: hard_blocking: synchronous call in the critical path; the dependent service cannot complete its operation without a response. async_event: subscribes to events published by this service; eventual consistency is acceptable. soft_query: non-blocking enrichment query; failure degrades but does not block. platform: infrastructure dependency (event bus, API gateway, IAM).

rationale.description: Why this dependency exists and what the dependent service uses from the dependency.

technology_constraints.description: Technology decisions or constraints that are fixed or strongly recommended for this service.

deployment_model.description: How the service is expected to be operated.

data_residency.description: UK GDPR / PRA data residency requirement for the service's primary data store.

latency_class.description: The dominant latency requirement for the service's primary operations. Drives infrastructure and deployment decisions.

availability_target.description: Target availability expressed as a percentage (e.g. 99.95%) or SLA tier. Derived from the operational resilience important business service impact tolerances where applicable.

pci_dss_scope.description: Whether this service is in scope for PCI DSS cardholder data environment (CDE) assessment.

regulatory_data_obligations.description: Specific data obligations applying to this service (e.g. PRA regulatory reporting data, FSCS eligibility data, PCI DSS cardholder data, UK GDPR personal data).

market_context.description: Build-vs-buy assessment and vendor landscape for this service. Informs the make/buy/partner decision for the service.

build_vs_buy_assessment.description: The recommended build-vs-buy posture. must_build: regulatory accountability, proprietary data, or competitive differentiation requires in-house build. strong_buy: commodity capability with specialist vendors that outcompete in-house builds. build_with_vendor_components: build the service boundary in-house but buy key components (ML models, connectivity infrastructure). buy_and_configure: buy a vendor platform and configure/extend it. saas_preferred: managed SaaS service with minimal customisation.

build_rationale.description: Rationale for the build-vs-buy decision, referencing capability file evidence.

vendor_options.description: Shortlisted vendor options where buy is recommended or considered.

fit_assessment.description: preferred: the recommended buy option. shortlisted: viable but not preferred. reference_only: noted as market context but not being evaluated.

notes.description: Any relevant notes on the vendor option, including UK market references, regulatory track record, or disqualifying factors.

design_decisions.description: Architectural design decisions specific to this service that are not captured in the capability file.

decision.description: A clear statement of the design decision.

rationale.description: Why this decision was made, including trade-offs considered.

rejected_because.description: Why the alternatives were not chosen.

examples.name: Retail Banking Core
examples.description: Realises the retained sub-capabilities of CAP-001: current accounts, savings and deposits, and personal lending. Owns the retail customer ledger, product configuration for deposit and credit products, and the Consumer Duty evidence trail for the retail customer base.

dependencies.rationale: Account creation requires KYC clearance from SVC-050 before the customer ledger record can be provisioned.

technology_constraints.data_residency: UK only — PRA FSCS eligibility data and retail customer PII

market_context.build_rationale: Core banking platform (Thought Machine Vault, Mambu, or 10x) provides the ledger and product factory. The bank must own the data model, regulatory reporting derivations, and Consumer Duty evidence trail layered over the bought core.

vendor_options.notes: UK references: Lloyds Banking Group (CAP-001 equivalent), Atom Bank, Monzo US. Cloud-native, API-first, smart contract product configuration. Highest implementation cost but strongest architecture alignment.
UK references: Santander UK (some products), OakNorth. Strong for loans and deposits; composable. Faster time-to-deploy than Thought Machine.
UK-built. JP Morgan Chase UK reference. Designed for incumbent transformation path.
